scope: Proposition 10.6 (Simultaneous segment counts) of the manuscript “The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4” (preprints/The-critical-Liouville-quantum-sphere-and-geometric-limits-of-FK-maps-at-q-equals-4-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b9236021eab20eb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 175. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Start a balanced recursion at pinit ≍ Bn and stop a branch when it first exceeds p∗ = C∗Bn. The probability of any such crossing tends to zero as C∗ → ∞. For every δ1 > 0, sufficiently small, the expected number of nodes with k = ⌊log(p∗/p)⌋ is at most Ce(2+δ1)k. With arbitrarily high probability, simultaneously for all ancestry lines and all k ≥ 0, the number of such nodes on any one line is at most Ceδ1k, with a suitable deterministic C.
